decision: defined done as six checks on the real phone: APK installs and starts, connects with an imported key and gets Claude's answer, phone layout with back gesture, reconnect after a minute in the background, signed APK in each release for Obtainium, suites green
why: the user asked for the Android build, and a long run needs a predicate to check against

decision: left out notifications while the app is closed, a terminal key row, and UI updates from the hub
why: each is its own follow-up; the OTA work runs in a separate fork

decision: order: Android project and first APK, device harness, SSH key on the phone, phone layout, reconnect, release pipeline
why: riskiest unknown first: building the Rust side for Android; the harness comes before the features it checks

decision: generated the Android project with tauri android init and built a debug APK for arm64 on the server
why: riskiest unknown first: the Rust SSH stack on Android with the NDK
evidence: commit c0f06f3; build log: 10 min 53 s cold, 197 MB debug APK
result: VERIFIED: installs on the Nord, starts, shows the connection settings, no FATAL in logcat

decision: handed the phone layout to a worker in its own worktree, with its own bridge and Vite ports, while the key flow is built here
why: the two touch different files, and separate ports keep their browser checks from colliding

decision: test login for the phone: a throwaway sshd on the server's loopback port 2422 with its own keys, reached from the phone through adb reverse
why: the user's sshd and authorized_keys stay untouched, and nothing opens to the internet
result: VERIFIED: the phone reads the SSH banner through the tunnel

decision: drive the real app on the phone with Playwright's Android support through the WebView's debugging socket
why: the same kind of checks as the browser suite, on the real device
result: VERIFIED: Playwright saw the connection dialog at 384x853

decision: on a phone the app keeps its own key: make one on the device (recommended, the private key never travels) or import an OpenSSH file, shown with its public key and fingerprint
why: a phone has no ~/.ssh; a key made on the phone means only its public half goes to the VPS
result: VERIFIED in tests: both kinds log in against a private sshd

decision: reset the app between device checks with run-as instead of pm clear
why: OnePlus refuses pm clear over adb (CLEAR_APP_USER_DATA), and run-as reaches only the debug build's own files

decision: wrapped the key fingerprint in the settings dialog
why: one long word stretched the dialog past the phone's width and cut it off
evidence: screenshot in the job folder, not committed
result: open until the device check passes

decision: the device check timed out on Save; a probe showed the button steady and frames running, but the keyboard covering it: the visible height fell to 600 of 853 px while the page kept its full height
why: tested the premise before a second fix: Tauri's activity turns on edge to edge, so the page draws under the bars and the keyboard

decision: MainActivity applies the system bar, cutout and keyboard insets as padding around the page
why: keeps content out from under the status bar and lifts the page above the keyboard; Android 15 enforces edge to edge, so windowSoftInputMode alone would not last
result: open until the device check passes

decision: device check passed after the insets fix
why: the predicate's second item, on the real phone
result: VERIFIED: key made on the phone, logged in, Claude answered a message sent from the phone

decision: first background check passed, but the server log showed one login: the connection had simply survived a minute with the screen on and charging
why: a pass that proves nothing about reconnecting; suspected the observation before trusting it

decision: the check now drops the app's connection on the server's side while the app is in the background, and requires a second login with the phone's key
why: makes the reconnect path run on the real phone
result: VERIFIED: logged in again and showed a session started meanwhile

decision: connect to the WebView by the running process's socket name
why: after a forced stop the old process's socket lingered and Playwright hung on it

decision: made one release signing key (RSA 4096, PKCS12, 100 years) in ~/.config/orfoni/android, readable only by root, with its password in a properties file Gradle reads only when ORFONI_ANDROID_SIGNING names it
why: Android installs an update only with the same signature, and developer verification binds the key; keeping it off the repo and out of CI means no secret travels
result: made; the user must back it up outside the server

decision: release APKs are built on the server and attached to the GitHub release the windows workflow made, at that release's version
why: the key stays on the server; the version code grows with the run number, which Obtainium needs

decision: reviewed and merged the worker's phone layout: one derived depth (list, conversation, sheet or terminal) with history following it, touch Enter adds a line, header folds into a row with More
why: single source of truth for navigation; Android back closes the front layer and leaves the app at the list
evidence: commits c403e65..998ec08; worker's 56 narrow checks and a 0-pixel desktop diff

decision: release APK built on the server and checked on the phone: signed with the new key, version 0.3.18 (code 3018), arm64, starts, makes a key, copies it, and logs in
why: the artifact the user installs, checked the same way as the debug build where Playwright cannot reach
evidence: apksigner verify; sshd log shows the release key's login

decision: fixed: phone keyboards capitalized the user field (root became Root)
why: found while typing into the release build over adb

decision: phone layout checked on the Nord: fits 384 px unzoomed on conversation, More and list, More holds the actions and selects, Android back returns to the list
why: the predicate's third item on the real device
evidence: android.spec.ts; phone screenshots in the git-ignored results

decision: Android back goes through browser history, one entry per layer, instead of Tauri's onBackButtonPress
why: registering the listener takes the gesture over completely, including leaving the app from the list; with history, Tauri's default back handling does the right thing at every depth

decision: the worker gave the task sheet and the terminal their own history entries, beyond the brief
why: back from a full-screen terminal would otherwise have left the conversation; accepted after review

decision: the root element carries the narrow class too
why: the connection dialogs render outside the app's layout and missed the touch sizes, which the worker reported

decision: device screenshots come from the phone (adb screencap), not through the WebView
why: Playwright's WebView screenshot came out tiled

decision: screenshots and logs from the phone stay in git-ignored or scratch folders, the shared screenshots show only test sessions, and the home address Tailscale showed is written nowhere
why: the user asked not to leak private details from the phone
evidence: memory note on the test phone

decision: full run: 732 unit tests, Rust tests, hub live 22 of 23, desktop Playwright 22 of 23, settings unchanged
why: the predicate's sixth item

decision: the desktop plan-window check passed when rerun alone; the hub restart check failed again
why: a failure that repeats is real; the hub journal showed it listening 4 s after the restart while the check waited 1.5 s

decision: the restart check now reconnects until the hub answers
why: the hub restoring sessions before it listens is a legitimate state, so waiting for it is a fix, not a guard

decision: made one release command, tools/release.sh
why: a release now has a second step on the server, which is easy to forget; a script beats a note
result: INCONCLUSIVE: its lookups work, the whole script first runs at the next release

decision: windows run 18 published v0.3.18; the signed APK at 0.3.18 was built from the final code, checked, and installed on the phone, but attaching it to the release was blocked by Claude Code's auto mode check
why: uploading to a public release is an outward action the check stopped; left for the user rather than worked around
result: open: needs the user to attach the APK or allow it
